Section: Introduction

1. "Welcome, aspiring guitarist. I'm Bertrand Laurence, your mentor for today's session. Over." (30 sec)

2. "We'll start at the very beginning, with your finger on the first fret, root note, ready to explore. Over." (30)

3. "Take a deep breath, relax your shoulders, and let the music flow through you. Très bien. Over." (30)

4. "Remember, learning guitar is a journey; enjoy each step, and we'll communicate using clear protocols. Over." (30)

5. "Let's begin by setting the intention: BE, DO, PLAY. Over." (30)

Section: BE-DO-PLAY

6. "First, BE: adopt a mindset of curiosity and openness, as if you're meeting an old friend. Over." (30)

7. "Feel the guitar against your body, notice the weight, the texture of the wood, and let that awareness ground you. Over." (30)

8. "Now, DO: we will translate that intention into a simple action—placing your index finger on the first fret of the low E string. Over." (30)

9. "Press down firmly, just behind the fret wire, and listen for a clear tone. Over." (30)

10. "If the note buzzes, adjust your finger angle; if it's muted, increase pressure slightly. Over." (30)

11. "Practice this BE-DO cycle: be present, do the placement, and notice the result. Over." (30)

12. "When you can produce a clean note consistently, we move to PLAY: let that note ring and resonate. Over." (30)

13. "Play it again, this time adding a gentle down‑stroke with your pick or thumb, feeling the vibration. Over." (30)

14. "Notice how the sound changes when you vary the attack—soft for a whisper, stronger for a statement. Over." (30)

Section: Net Protocol (Over / Ready / Copy / Go ahead)

15. "Now let's introduce the Net Protocol, a simple communication loop that keeps our practice flowing without needing to look at a screen. Over." (30)

16. "The protocol has four words: Over, Ready, Copy, Go ahead. Over." (30)

17. "When I finish a sentence, I say 'Over' to signal that I've completed my turn. Over." (30)

18. "You respond with 'Ready' to show you're prepared to receive the next instruction. Over." (30)

19. "I then say 'Copy' to confirm I've heard your acknowledgment, and you reply 'Go ahead' to indicate you're ready for me to continue. Over." (30)

20. "This loop creates a hands‑free rhythm: Over, Ready, Copy, Go ahead, then repeat. Over." (30)

21. "Let's try it now: I'll say a short cue, then wait for your response. Over." (30)

22. "Cue: Place your finger on the second fret, G string. Over." (30)

23. (Student would respond Ready, but we just continue script) "Your turn: say 'Ready' when you're set. Over." (30)

24. "I'll then say 'Copy' to acknowledge, and you'll say 'Go ahead' to proceed. Over." (30)

25. "We'll use this pattern throughout the lesson to keep navigation smooth and eyes‑free. Over." (30)

Section: Hands-free Navigation

26. "Hands‑free navigation means we rely on audio cues and the Net Protocol instead of looking at a chart or phone. Over." (30)

27. "Your ears become your guide; each instruction tells you where to move next. Over." (30)

28. "For example, after you play the first‑fret root note, I'll cue: 'Shift to the third fret, same string.' Over." (30)

29. "You'll respond Ready, I'll say Copy, you'll say Go ahead, and then you'll move. Over." (30)

30. "This method builds muscle memory and auditory awareness, essential for playing without visual dependence. Over." (30)

31. "Let's practice a simple sequence: first‑fret E, then third‑fret G, then fifth‑fret B, all on the low E string. Over." (30)

32. "I'll give each step, you'll follow the protocol, and we'll keep the flow going. Over." (30)

33. "Remember to keep your tone even and your breathing steady as you navigate. Over." (30)

34. "If you ever feel lost, simply say 'Ready' and I'll repeat the last cue. Over." (30)

Section: Putting It All Together

35. "Now we combine BE-DO-PLAY, the Net Protocol, and hands‑free navigation into a mini‑song. Over." (30)

36. "We'll play a four‑note motif: E (1st fret), G (3rd fret), B (5th fret), D (7th fret) on the low E string, then reverse. Over." (30)

37. "Start with BE: feel ready, DO: place your finger, PLAY: let the note sing, all while using Over, Ready, Copy, Go ahead. Over." (30)

38. "I'll cue each fret shift; you'll respond with the protocol and execute the move. Over." (30)

39. "Let's begin: Over." (30)
